title: LicoUp usage observation
description: One observation from one usage source. The source, the instance and the authority are bound by the host at the transport, never asserted here. Correction raises `revision`; `retract` withdraws this observation and nothing else. An unknown metric carries no number, because a zero would be a claim that nothing happened.

revision.description: Stable within one source epoch. A strictly higher revision replaces a lower one; equal or lower revisions never do.

operation.description: `upsert` reports or revises; `retract` withdraws this observation. A retraction cannot offset another source's usage.

sourceEpoch.description: Reset and replay defence. A new epoch starts new cumulative series.

scopeRef.description: An invocation or an authorized aggregate read range, issued by the host. It is what keeps a producer from attaching itself to another user's run.

observedAt.description: UTC as the producer saw it. An anomalous clock is preserved as the source's own fact and never overrides the host's monotonic clock.

intervalStart.description: The start of the window, or of the cumulative series. Two cumulative readings are comparable only within one epoch, one metric and one origin.

metrics.description: Namespaced metric to reading. At least one on an upsert, and none on a retraction.

value.description: Exact decimal text, never a JSON number, so no consumer can round it. Null when the quality is unknown.

quality.description: What the producer says about its own value. A producer reporting `reported` gains no settlement authority from saying so.

includes.description: Metrics this reading already contains, so a total is never added to its own subset.

cost.description: An estimate or a report, never an assertion about the user's budget.

amount.description: Exact decimal text. Binary floating point never enters a ledger.
